subject: CrestPoint: Concurrency spike -> RCA, mitigation plan, exec commitments
messages:
From: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jmills@crestpointlogistics.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden errors & degraded throughput - morning of 5/29

Sergio —

Morning. We started seeing elevated 500 errors and request queueing across our peak routes starting ~09:40 PT this morning. Latency spiked to 2.6s p95 for our shipment-summary calls and throughput dropped ~30% compared to yesterday. This caused cascading backoffs in our service and a partial feature outage for a subset of users.

Attached are two sample request traces and a small CSV of request rates. We’re in a bind for an upcoming demo; need ETA on remediation and short-term mitigation.

Please advise immediate next steps and whether you can escalate to an exec if capacity adjustments / hotfixes are required.

Thanks,
Cara Lin
Head of Integrations
CrestPoint Logistics

Attachments: request-trace-1.txt (text), request-trace-2.txt (text), summary-rates-0529.csv (CSV)

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>
Cc: Jordan Mills <jmills@crestpointlogistics.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden errors & degraded throughput - morning of 5/29

Cara —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the traces, we’re on it. I’m standing up a short bridge with eng now to triage (will share link). Initial ask: can you confirm the rate pattern (burst vs sustained) for the affected tenant IDs and whether any config changes were rolled out from your side around 08:50–09:30 PT?

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Bridge with infra + serving runtime to capture live metrics and scale targets.
- Short-term mitigation: enable burst capacity for your Dedicated pool and increase autoscale floor if needed.
- Post-incident: deliver RCA and concrete action plan by Monday EOD with exec-level note and remediation timeline.

I’ll loop in Laura and Kim to own cross-org commitments and any SLA credits/runbook updates.

Bridge link (active): https://meet.redwood/bridge/CP-0421-0529 (joining now).

—Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: concurrency-metrics-05-29.csv (uploaded to drive)

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@crestpointlogistics.com>
Date: Sat, 29 May 2027 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden errors & degraded throughput - morning of 5/29

Team —

Joined the bridge. Quick notes from ops after a 30-minute triage:
- Root trigger: a short-lived client-side retry storm from a misconfigured background job at CrestPoint that created ~3x concurrent fanout to the inference route between 09:12–09:48 PT.
- Serving runtime reacted as designed (queueing + shedding) but several mitigations we have in prod (prefix KV cache, partial result path) were not sufficient to keep p95 under the SLA.
- Immediate mitigation executed: temporarily enabled crestpoint’s burst reserve and increased shard count for the route (10% capacity add) which reduced 500s and normalized throughput by ~10:10 PT.

Condition now: stable but we recommended CrestPoint throttle/release fix on their job and we’ll produce a write-up and permanent configuration change to autoscale policy for sustained bursts.

I’m producing the preliminary RCA and action tracker — I’ll attach it to this thread and kick it to Kim and Markus for remediation workstreams.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@crestpointlogistics.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Preliminary RCA and corrective actions (draft)

Hi all —

Attached is a short RCA draft (crestpoint_rca_v1.pdf) and a CSV of the concurrency samples. Key points summarized:
1) Trigger: client-side scheduled job misfire at CrestPoint produced bursty concurrency (approx 8k req/min sustained for 38 minutes).
2) System response: our serving runtime correctly queued and shed load, but autoscale policy did not ramp fast enough given the request profile and the current shard-sizing for that route.
3) Immediate fixes applied: temporary shard increase, burst reserve enablement — reduced errors to baseline by ~09:58 PT.

Action items (owners and timelines):
- CrestPoint: patch scheduled job and add client-side rate limiter (Cara, ETA 6/1 EOD).
- Redwood Runtime: change autoscale policy to include a faster short-window ramp for peak bursts (Markus, ETA 6/7).
- Redwood Dedicated: expand max shard buffer for high-concurrency tenants and create guardrail to auto-enable burst reserve when queue depth > threshold (Kim, ETA 6/4).
- CS/Eng: customer-facing postmortem and exec summary delivered + offer of one-week free burst credit (Sergio/Laura, ETA 6/2).

Please review the draft and flag any missing items. I’ll finalize the RCA and add runbook changes after confirmation.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: crestpoint_rca_v1.pdf, concurrency-metrics-05-29.csv

From: markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Cc: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preliminary RCA and corrective actions (draft)

Thanks Kim —

Reviewed the draft. I’ve opened two internal PRs:
- autoscale: add short-window ramp factor + threshold (PR#7842)
- dedicated: shard buffer guardrail + burst-reserve auto trigger (PR#7845)

Workplan:
- Code & QA: 6/1–6/4 (engineering sprint), staging tests 6/5, rollout to canary 6/6, full rollout 6/7.
- I’ll also add a telemetry alert (queue-depth sustained > X for 10m) to trigger a proactive notification to CS and the customer.

Markus

From: sergio_alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Cara Lin <cara@crestpointlogistics.com>, Jordan Mills <jmills@crestpointlogistics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, markus_klein <markus@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: CrestPoint post-incident summary, commitments, and next steps

Cara / Jordan —

Thanks again for patience while we conducted the triage and hardening work. This message summarizes both what happened and the commitments we’re making on timelines. Attached: final RCA (crestpoint_rca_v1.pdf) and an action tracker with owners.

Executive summary:
- What: a misconfigured background job at CrestPoint produced a short retry storm (09:12–09:48 PT, 5/29) that generated ~3x expected concurrency and pushed the route past current autoscale ramping behaviors.
- Impact: elevated 500s, p95 latency to 2.6s, throughput down ~30% for approximately 36 minutes. No data compromise.
- Immediate remediation: burst reserve enabled + temporary shard increase restored normal service by ~09:58 PT.

Commitments (owner / target):
- CrestPoint: patch job + client-side backoff (Cara) — 2027-06-01 EOD (confirmed done).
- Redwood Runtime (Markus): short-window autoscale ramp + telemetry alert — prod rollout target 2027-06-07 (in progress).
- Redwood Dedicated (Kim): permanent guardrail for shard buffer + burst auto-enable — prod target 2027-06-04.
- CS (Sergio/Laura): customer exec note + one-week complimentary burst credit applied — completed 2027-06-01.

Follow-up plan: weekly check-ins for two weeks (first sync 2027-06-03) to confirm stability metrics; we’ll share an interim metrics report after canary rollout and a final post-implementation verification.

If you’d like an exec-level readout with our CTO or Head of Revenue, I can schedule a 30-min briefing next week — suggested times Wed/Thu 10–12 PT.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
